slots.title: Support for amplitude-scaling measured records
slots.instruction: Assess what support exists in blasting, geotechnical earthquake engineering, or transient dynamic analysis literature for amplitude-scaling measured records for scenario studies. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Preserved and non-preserved properties
slots.instruction: Explain which properties simple amplitude scaling preserves and which properties it does not preserve, including frequency content, duration, phase relationships, component coherency, wave propagation effects, source/path/site terms, cycle count, and pore-pressure-relevant cumulative demand. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Independent component-peak scaling assumptions and limitations
slots.instruction: State the assumptions and limitations that should be declared for TSF dynamic response assessment when measured records are scaled independently by component peaks. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Distinction from other waveform-adjustment methods
slots.instruction: Explain how amplitude scaling differs from spectral matching, target-spectrum adjustment, synthetic waveform generation, and calibrated blast source modelling. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Defensible wording for scenario demand histories
slots.instruction: Develop defensible wording for describing scaled measured blast records as scenario demand histories for saturated-tailings response. Write in flowing paragraphs.

constraints: The output is for an English technical report.
The work must construct scenario records for TSF dynamic response review, not perform spectral matching.
The work must not synthesize a physics-based blast source.
The work must not claim direct pore-pressure prediction from acceleration records alone.
